hits.full_text: If you want to start writing, the greatest thing you can do is block off 1 hour every morning and stick to it. Absolutely no exposure to other opinions or distractions (social media, messages, phone). You need space for creative ideas and modern life is great at taking that from you.
hits.hook: thedankoe: block off 1 morning hour for writing, no phone/opinions; space for creative ideas (best brand fit today)
hits.draft_en:
The hardest part of writing isn't the writing.

It's keeping the phone in another room for an hour and letting the page be the only thing that talks back.
hits.video_tip: 12 seconds, no face. Soft morning window light on a wooden desk. A phone is placed face-down and slid out of frame. A fountain pen uncapped on textured cream paper. Hand writes three lines, pauses, keeps going. Room sound only. Last frame text: 'One protected hour.'

hits.full_text: Underrated relationship advice: Stop keeping score. Who called last. Who picked up the last check. Who apologized. Who did more. Whatever. Healthy relationships aren’t always 50/50. Sometimes they’re 90/10. Sometimes 25/75. They just need to add up to 100. It’s a partnership.

hits.draft_en:
Keeping score wears everyone out. Who texted last. Who did more. Who apologized first.

I'd rather be the one who just shows up with coffee and doesn't check the ledger.
hits.video_tip: 10 seconds, no face. Two mismatched mugs on a cream napkin; a hand sets down a second coffee without a note or tally. Room sound. Last frame text: 'No ledger.'

hits.full_text: Two ways to feel richer: Earn More or Want Less. Everyone obsesses over the first. Nobody talks about the second. The person who falls in love with a simple life escapes the comparison traps that keep everyone on the treadmill. They’re free. Which was the real goal all along.

hits.draft_en:
There are two ways to feel like you have enough.

Earn more, or want less.

I keep choosing the second. Three colors on a site. One good pen. A desk that doesn't need to impress anyone.
hits.video_tip: 10 seconds, overhead. Three swatches on textured cream — black, cream, vampire red — then a fountain pen laid beside them. No face, room sound. Last frame text: 'Want less.'

reply_ideas.reply_text: The phone in another room is the whole trick. Once it's out of reach, the page stops competing with everyone else's opinion of what I should be writing.
The scorekeeping is exhausting even when you're "winning." I'd rather be slightly uneven and warm than perfectly even and tired.
Wanting less is the quieter flex. Three colors. One desk. A pen that already works. The treadmill doesn't have a finish line anyway.
Writing is still the only place I can tell if an idea is real or just loud. Halfway down the page it either holds or it doesn't.
